learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the difference between incomplete word groups and complete thoughts by mastering phrases and clauses!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A phrase is a group of words that makes some sense but not complete sense. It does not have a Subject and a Verb together, like 'in the park' or 'a beautiful sunny day'.
A clause is a group of words that contains both a Subject and a Verb! It is like a mini-sentence inside a bigger sentence, like 'because she was tired' or 'the dog barked loudly'.
An independent clause is the boss! It has a subject, a verb, and makes complete sense all by itself. It can stand alone as a perfect, complete sentence.
A dependent clause has a subject and a verb, but it feels incomplete. It starts with words like 'because', 'when', or 'if', and it needs to hold hands with an independent clause to make full sense!

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ Phrase or Clause Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Open your favorite storybook and hunt for clues! Find and write down three phrases and three clauses on a piece of paper.

quick_recap: ⭐ Phrases are missing a subject or a verb, so they never make a complete sentence.
⭐ Clauses have both a subject and a verb; independent clauses can stand alone, but dependent clauses cannot!
